docs.text: The Lake Erie Chemical Company, based in Ohio.
The bitter rival to Lake Erie Chemical Co was Federal Laboratories, originally based in Pittsburgh, PA.

The primary product line for both companies (Lake Erie and Federal) was, in fact, guns and ammunition. You read that right. Firearms that were designed to shoot tear gas munitions. Then the munitions containing CS. And then tear gas cartridges for other manufacturer's firearms.
Lake Erie Chemical Co was founded by Colonel Byron Cassius "Biff" Goss, latterly of the Chemical Warfare Service and a wartime buddy of Fries.
Here's an example of the very similar rival product from Lake Erie Chemical. As you can see, these are, in effect, large bore shotguns.

As another aside, Federal Labs and Lake Erie Chemical were the inspiration for the US military M79 grenade launcher, 40mm. Neither got the contract to make it, but I suspect (need to research it) either or both got contracts to make 40mm CS projectiles for it, or at least made the CS

It should be noted that both Lake Erie and Federal Labs "gas guns" are simple, physically robust firearms, typical of their era, and will last a century or more in service. They turn up all over the world.

To summarise where I left off, the American self-defence tear gas market was, in its development, fundamentally a sideline business from two tear-gas-centric firearms companies, Federal Labs and Lake Erie Chemical
So, it's the late 1960s and there are now three big names in the US tear gas business: Smith & Wesson, Federal Laboratories, and Lake Erie Chemical. All three of them, at heart, gun companies.
You got it! Lake Erie Chemical gets bought by Bangor Punta! It becomes the chemical division of Smith and Wesson. Note the "Mace" being sold, bottom left, on the advert.
Oh wait, there's really only two companies.... Guess who buys out the venerable Lake Erie Chemical Company....
So, what happened to Lake Erie Chemical Company (now S&W Chemical) and Federal Laboratories?
Actually, Smith and Wesson started the big boom in the "self-defence" spray industry. They bought Mace and ran a whole tear gas factor called Great Lakes Chemical.
Smith and Wesson literally bought General Ordance Equipment Co in the 1960s. S&W also ran Lake Erie Chemical, which made no end of tear gas munitions.

It is the basis of halon type fire suppression, although that fell into disuse trying to save the ozone layer. A company called Great Lakes Chemical was a Fortune 500 prior to its sale and was built on bromine products. Its corporate headquarters was about 200 yards from my house right now.
The Pulmosan No. 1750 setup was also sold by Lake Erie Chemical Company as the No. 45, for protection against riot gasses, one of their main products.

On 11 Nov 1918, using the RR spur line from the secret production facility at Willoughby, OH, the near total product of Lewisite was run into Lake Erie and dumped. The US Army Chemical Corps workers at the Willoughby site then left the site, never to return.
